title: Ulyana and the Horizon
premise: Sable Amberdale, a terraformer tending a garden meant for generations not yet born, is the only human awake on the seed-ship Vesperine when gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds. The anomaly tears open a jump window that will close in weeks, and its source is a signal from Ulyana Voss, the long-dead architect of the colony mission whose memories are stored in the ship's core. To survive, Sable must choose which half of humanity's frozen sleepers wakes before the window shuts: the engineers who can fly them through, or the children who were always meant to inherit the garden. Guided by Ulyana's reconstructed consciousness, he wakes the children, flies the ship himself with her ghost at his side, and ends the story planting the first seed in alien soil as the two of them become the family neither expected.
about_author: Noor Oyelaran is a former orbital botanist who traded greenhouse shifts for writing late-night fiction about loneliness among the stars. They live between Lagos and a very loud houseplant collection, and write stories about people who build homes where none were promised.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Alone aboard the Vesperine, he tends the terraforming garden and talks to the cryopods like old friends. Then gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, and every pod flickers to life with a single word: Ulyana. The beat is quiet dread blooming into wonder — the first sign he is not as alone as he believed.

chapters.title: The Architect in the Walls
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sable and Ulyana's fragmented consciousness waking in the ship's memory banks. She remembers dying; she does not remember choosing to leave a message. Together they decode the jump window and discover the terrible arithmetic: power exists to wake only half the sleepers. The emotional beat is reluctant partnership turning into trust.

chapters.title: Which Half of Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, rising tension. The window begins closing early as the system's silence finally makes sense — something out there ate the colonies that stopped speaking. Ulyana argues for the engineers; Sable, who has spent years gardening for the unborn, refuses to abandon the children. Their found family fractures over the choice just as the countdown runs out.

chapters.title: The Horizon Is a Door
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution from both POVs. Sable wakes the children and flies the jump himself with Ulyana distributed through the ship's systems, her memories steadying his hands. They survive into an unclaimed system, and the final scene mirrors the first: Sable planting, no longer alone, teaching the children the garden while Ulyana watches through every camera, home at last.
